sources.title: Nobel Winner John Jumper to Leave Google DeepMind for Anthropic
How an 'accidental chemist' honed his approach at UChicago on the way to a Nobel Prize
sources.quote_checked: When I started, I knew no chemistry. None. | As an 'accidental chemist,' I wanted to go from understanding a very narrow slice of the problem | I'm a big believer in interdisciplinary science. | Nature is complex, and I think neural networks can handle complexity in surprisingly useful ways.

sources.title: Q&A: Alumnus John Jumper, winner of 2024 Chemistry Nobel Prize
sources.quote_checked: I think to be a researcher you really want to be a researcher in an area that's ready to make big breakthroughs. | It's a lot more fun to chase the constant failure and occasional success of science in a group | Ultimately, we want this tool to help experimental scientists do better experiments. | I would love it if AlphaFold were the second most important thing I was known for. | I think whether it makes us better at many problems or a few well-suited problems, we'll find out in five or 10 years.

sources.title: Google DeepMind's AlphaFold is becoming AI's killer app for science
sources.quote_checked: The impact has really exceeded all of our expectations | It is just a part of training to be a molecular biologist | The really exciting dataset and the really big dataset is the entirety of the scientific literature

sources.title: Google DeepMind's John Jumper on winning the Nobel Prize and the future of AlphaFold
sources.quote_checked: I really didn't think it was going to happen
